passages.title: Two sons seek David's throne
passages.summary: Adonijah gathers supporters at En Rogel. Bathsheba and Nathan approach David, who orders Solomon’s anointing at Gihon. Bathsheba and Nathan act before Adonijah can secure the throne. David publicly names Solomon as the next king.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: Who speaks for Solomon when David must choose the next king?

passages.title: David dies and Solomon consolidates power
passages.summary: David gives final instructions. Solomon removes Abiathar and orders the deaths of Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei. Solomon secures his rule by removing rivals. His orders include deaths and the loss of Abiathar’s priestly office.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: How does Solomon explain his orders against each rival?

passages.title: Solomon asks for wisdom and judges a dispute
passages.summary: At Gibeon, Solomon asks for an understanding heart. In Jerusalem, two women dispute the identity of a living infant. One woman would rather lose the child than see him killed. Solomon recognizes her care.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me encourages seeking discernment between right and wrong.

passages.title: Officials, provisions, and wisdom
passages.summary: The chapter lists officials, regional suppliers, royal provisions, and Solomon’s reputation for wisdom. Solomon’s court needs food from across the kingdom. Local officers supply the king and his household.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: Who provides the food that supports Solomon’s court?

passages.title: Hiram supplies timber for the temple
passages.summary: Solomon and Hiram arrange timber and food exchanges. Adoniram supervises a labor levy, while builders prepare stone and wood. Hiram supplies wood and skilled help. Solomon also forces men to work on the building project.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: What does temple building require from the workers and their families?

passages.title: The temple is built
passages.summary: The account describes the temple’s rooms, wooden carvings, gold covering, and cherubim. God’s promise also requires faithful conduct. Cedar walls, carved flowers, and separate rooms mark the temple. Its design sets worship apart.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me invites reflection on sacred space and temple symbols.

passages.title: Royal buildings and bronze furnishings
passages.summary: Solomon’s palace buildings are described. Hiram the bronze worker makes pillars, the sea, movable stands, and other vessels. Hiram the artisan is distinct from the king of Tyre. The chapter describes craft knowledge and materials alongside royal buildings.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older Church manual compares the bronze sea with baptism.

passages.title: The ark enters the temple and Solomon prays
passages.summary: The ark is brought into the sanctuary. Solomon prays about justice, forgiveness, drought, foreigners, war, and exile. The prayer says heaven cannot contain God. It joins a particular sacred house with concern for people beyond Israel.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me connects the dedication prayer with temple covenants and walking in God’s ways.

passages.title: Promises, warnings, labor, and trade
passages.summary: God answers Solomon with a promise and warning. The chapter describes towns, building projects, labor, and ships sailing toward Ophir. God’s promise calls for continued faithfulness. Solomon’s buildings and trade also depend on workers and foreign help.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies God’s promises and the responsibility to keep covenants.

passages.title: The queen of Sheba visits
passages.summary: The queen tests Solomon with questions and sees the court. Gifts, trade, gold, horses, and royal wealth follow. The queen tests Solomon’s wisdom with questions. His answers and wealth impress her.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: What impresses the queen besides Solomon’s wealth?

passages.title: Solomon turns away and adversaries rise
passages.summary: Solomon supports other gods. Hadad and Rezon become adversaries. Ahijah promises Jeroboam a kingdom, and Solomon later dies. Solomon's choices weaken his kingdom. God promises most tribes to Jeroboam.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me asks readers to examine influences that turn their hearts from God.

passages.title: Rehoboam rejects the petition and the kingdom divides
passages.summary: Rehoboam rejects advice to ease the people’s burden. The northern tribes follow Jeroboam, who establishes worship at Bethel and Dan. Rehoboam's threats divide the kingdom. Jeroboam then builds places of worship to keep people from Jerusalem.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies the effect of leaders’ choices and the need for good counsel.

passages.title: A man of God confronts Bethel
passages.summary: A man of God announces judgment at Bethel. An older prophet deceives him into eating, and a lion later kills him. An older prophet lies about God’s command. The visiting prophet trusts him and dies on his way home.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: Why does the visiting prophet accept a claim that changes his earlier command?

passages.title: Ahijah speaks and Shishak attacks Jerusalem
passages.summary: Jeroboam’s disguised wife visits Ahijah about their son Abijah. The child dies. The account then describes Rehoboam’s rule and Shishak’s attack. Jeroboam's wife seeks help for their sick child. Ahijah's warning reaches the whole royal family.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: How does Ahijah’s message affect Jeroboam’s wife and child?

passages.title: Judah’s rulers and a new northern dynasty
passages.summary: Abijam and Asa rule Judah. Asa seeks Ben Hadad’s help against Baasha. Baasha kills Nadab and destroys Jeroboam’s household. The kings make different choices about worship. Their wars also shape life in both kingdoms.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: What does Asa give away to gain help against Baasha?

passages.title: Kings fall before Omri and Ahab rise
passages.summary: Jehu condemns Baasha’s house. Zimri kills Elah and is defeated. Omri prevails over Tibni, builds Samaria, and is succeeded by Ahab. Plots and battles bring rapid changes of kings. Ahab’s marriage to Jezebel leads into Elijah’s story.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: How do the changes of kings affect their families and towns?

passages.title: Elijah and the widow at Zarephath
passages.summary: Elijah announces drought, receives food at Cherith, and stays with a widow at Zarephath. Her food endures, and her son returns to life. The widow shares food despite her fear of hunger. Her later grief leads her to question Elijah.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies the widow’s trust amid scarcity.

passages.title: Elijah confronts Ahab at Carmel
passages.summary: Obadiah meets Elijah. Elijah asks Israel to choose between God and Baal. Fire answers his prayer. Baal's prophets are killed, and rain returns. The people must choose whom to worship. Fire answers Elijah’s prayer. The victory also ends in killing Baal’s prophets.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me uses Elijah’s challenge to examine commitment to God.

passages.title: Elijah receives care and calls Elisha
passages.summary: Threatened by Jezebel, Elijah flees, asks to die, receives food, and travels to Horeb. He receives renewed work and places his mantle on Elisha. Elijah needs food and rest before his next task. God gives him help and new work.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies the quiet voice and Elisha’s willingness to respond.

passages.title: Ahab defeats Ben Hadad and releases him
passages.summary: Ben Hadad attacks Samaria. Prophets advise Ahab, and Israel wins two battles. Ahab releases his opponent and receives a prophetic rebuke. Ahab wins two battles but spares Ben Hadad. A prophet warns him about that choice.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: Why does the prophet challenge Ahab after his victory?

passages.title: Naboth is killed and Elijah confronts Ahab
passages.summary: Naboth refuses to give up his vineyard. Jezebel arranges false accusations and his killing. Ahab takes possession, and Elijah announces judgment. Officials use false witnesses to kill Naboth. Ahab takes the inherited vineyard Naboth refused to sell.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: How does Ahab gain from Jezebel’s plot against Naboth?

passages.title: Micaiah warns Ahab before the final battle
passages.summary: Ahab and Jehoshaphat seek counsel about Ramoth Gilead. Micaiah describes a heavenly council and predicts defeat. Ahab dies in battle. Most prophets promise Ahab victory. Micaiah describes a heavenly meeting that reveals their deception.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older Church manual reads the lying spirit as God allowing deception.

guides.title: Study 1 Kings
guides.description: Follow selected chapters through the book.

steps.title: Two sons seek David's throne
steps.text: Adonijah gathers supporters at En Rogel. Bathsheba and Nathan approach David, who orders Solomon’s anointing at Gihon. Bathsheba and Nathan act before Adonijah can secure the throne. David publicly names Solomon as the next king.

steps.title: Rehoboam rejects the petition and the kingdom divides
steps.text: Rehoboam rejects advice to ease the people’s burden. The northern tribes follow Jeroboam, who establishes worship at Bethel and Dan. Rehoboam's threats divide the kingdom. Jeroboam then builds places of worship to keep people from Jerusalem.

steps.title: Micaiah warns Ahab before the final battle
steps.text: Ahab and Jehoshaphat seek counsel about Ramoth Gilead. Micaiah describes a heavenly council and predicts defeat. Ahab dies in battle. Most prophets promise Ahab victory. Micaiah describes a heavenly meeting that reveals their deception.
